newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico asks for NAFTA dispute panel in broom row.
newsitem.headline: Mexico asks for NAFTA dispute panel in broom row.

text.p: Mexico on Tuesday asked for the establishment of a dispute resolution panel under terms of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) following a new U.S. duty against Mexican millet broom imports.

The Commerce Ministry said in a statement that it will ask for the panel to be established following a U.S. move last November to raise import duties on Mexican millet broom imports to 33 percent from about 10 percent.
The United States applied the duty after arguing that the Mexican imports were causing excessive damage to the U.S. broom industry.
Mexico on Tuesday said the U.S. decision was mistaken.

"Mexico considers that the duty applied by the United States is contrary to the dispositions of NAFTA," the ministry said. "The investigation excluded from its consideration of damage to the industry other types of brooms, such as plastic, that compete with millet brooms."
Mexico said that it plans to keep higher import duties on about eight U.S. products, a move it took in December, until the broom dispute is settled.

A U.S. quota allows 100,000 dozen brooms to enter duty free per year. Last year, the city of Cadereyta, near the northern city of Monterrey, alone exported 700,000 dozen millet brooms to the United States, according to industry figures.
